title: Resilience research must cover every jurisdiction of possible exposure while weighting effort toward likely risk
content:
A.2.10.1.1 places a standing duty on the Core Facilitator to ensure "resilience research and preparedness efforts are continuously maintained," with a two-part allocation rule: projects "must generally be broadly diversified across all jurisdictions where the Sky Ecosystem could be directly or indirectly exposed, but efforts and resources must be prioritized towards jurisdictions where risks are more likely to emerge."

The two halves guard against opposite failure modes. Pure risk-weighting would concentrate everything on the obvious jurisdictions (US securities enforcement, say) and leave the ecosystem with no groundwork anywhere else — which is exactly where a surprise action lands hardest, because preparation cannot be improvised at speed. Pure diversification would spread a modest annual budget so thin that nothing usable is produced anywhere.

The operative phrase is "directly or indirectly exposed." Indirect exposure means Sky's research scope is set by where its users, integrators, Agents, and counterparties operate, not by where Sky itself has presence. For a permissionless stablecoin, that is effectively everywhere, so the diversification mandate is unbounded in principle and rationed in practice by budget.

The annotation at A.2.10.1.1.0.3.1 fills in what the work consists of — monitoring legal trends and regulatory changes, scenario planning and risk modeling, and developing mitigation strategies — confirming this is anticipatory research rather than response to live matters, which is handled by the Resilience Fund and the SOPs.
description: The Core Facilitator must keep the effort continuous and broadly diversified across all jurisdictions where Sky is directly or indirectly exposed, but prioritize where risks are more likely to emerge.
